classification.difficultyReason: Build two elevation equations from the distances, eliminate height to obtain a double-angle relation, and use the acute geometry to select the valid angle and height.

content.prompt:
An observer stands at point $A$ on flat ground and looks up at the top of a vertical tower of height $h$ metres with angle of elevation $\theta$. The observer walks 100 metres directly towards the tower to point $B$. At this position, which is 50 metres from the base of the tower, the angle of elevation is doubled.

Find the value of $\theta$ and hence, the height of the tower.

answer.short:
$\theta=30^\circ$, $h=50\sqrt3\text{ m}$.

Use $\tan2\theta=3\tan\theta$ and the tangent double-angle identity.
answer.worked:
The distances from the tower are 150 m at $A$ and 50 m at $B$. Both elevation angles are acute, so $0^\circ<\theta<45^\circ$.

$$\begin{align*}\tan\theta&=\frac{h}{150}\\\tan2\theta&=\frac{h}{50}\\\tan2\theta&=3\tan\theta\end{align*}$$

Let $t=\tan\theta$, where $t>0$.

$$\begin{align*}\frac{2t}{1-t^2}&=3t\\2t&=3t(1-t^2)\\2&=3-3t^2\\t^2&=\frac13\\t&=\frac1{\sqrt3}\\\theta&=30^\circ\\h&=150\tan30^\circ\\h&=50\sqrt3\text{ m}\end{align*}$$
